title: Present perfect vs past simple
titleVi: Hiện tại hoàn thành và quá khứ đơn
summary: Chọn đúng thì khi kể trải nghiệm, nêu số liệu và mô tả xu hướng — lỗi phổ biến nhất của band 6.5.
whyItMatters: Trong Writing Task 2, bạn liên tục phải nói về xu hướng kéo dài đến hiện tại (*Rents have risen since 2010*) và về sự kiện đã kết thúc (*The government raised the tax in 2019*). Trộn hai thì này là lỗi ngữ pháp khiến giám khảo khó cho điểm Grammatical Range & Accuracy trên 7.0, dù ý tưởng của bạn tốt.

sections.heading: The core difference: finished time vs unfinished time
body: The present perfect (**have/has + past participle**) connects a past action to *now*. The past simple (**verb + -ed / irregular form**) places the action entirely in the past.

Ask yourself one question before you choose: **is the time period finished or unfinished?** *Yesterday*, *in 2019*, *last century* are finished — use the past simple. *Since 2010*, *so far*, *over the past decade*, *this year* are unfinished — use the present perfect.
This is why you cannot say *I have visited Hue in 2018*: the year 2018 is closed, so the present perfect has nothing to connect to.

examples.right: The city has invested heavily in public transport since 2015.
examples.wrong: The city invested heavily in public transport since 2015.
examples.note: **since 2015** reaches into the present, so the period is unfinished.

examples.right: The city invested heavily in public transport in 2015.
examples.note: **in 2015** is a finished point in time.

examples.right: Unemployment has fallen by 3% over the past five years.
examples.wrong: Unemployment fell by 3% over the past five years.
examples.note: **over the past five years** continues up to now.

sections.heading: Time markers that decide the tense
body: Most exam errors come from ignoring the time marker. Learn these two lists as pairs — they are the fastest way to check a sentence in the exam.
One important exception: **just**, **already** and **yet** belong to the present perfect in British English, while **ago** always takes the past simple.

rows: so far / up to now / to date
over the past decade / recently / lately

sections.heading: Experience, result and news
body: Use the present perfect for **experience** when you do not say when: *Few policymakers have addressed the housing crisis.* Add *ever/never* for the first or zero occurrence: *This is the highest figure the survey has ever recorded.*
Use it for a **result that matters now**: *The council has closed the road* (= it is closed now). Compare *The council closed the road* (= a fact about the past; it may be open again).
Use the past simple for **finished narratives**: *In 2020 the council closed the road for six months.*

examples.right: Researchers have found a strong link between screen time and poor sleep.
examples.note: New finding, no time given — present perfect.

examples.right: Researchers found a strong link in a 2019 study.
examples.note: The study is a finished event.

examples.right: I have never seen such a rapid decline in birth rates.

sections.heading: Duration: for, since and the continuous form
body: **for** + a length of time (*for a decade*), **since** + a starting point (*since 2012*). Both need the present perfect when the situation continues.

When you want to stress that the activity is still going on — or that it explains a present result — use the present perfect continuous: *House prices have been rising steadily since 2016.* The simple form sounds more like a completed statistic; the continuous form emphasises the ongoing process, which is exactly the tone IELTS examiners reward in trend descriptions.
Stative verbs (know, believe, own, consist of) normally stay in the simple form: *The committee has known about the risk for years.*

rows: The population has been growing since 2005.
The population grew by 12% between 2005 and 2015.

sections.heading: In IELTS Task 1: choosing between the two
body: Task 1 graphs usually show a period that ends in the past, so the **past simple is the default**: *Sales rose sharply between 2010 and 2015.*

Switch to the present perfect only when the data clearly runs up to the present or the chart has no end date: *Sales have climbed steadily since 2018.* Never mix the two inside one description of the same period — inconsistency reads as a grammar error even when each sentence is individually correct.

examples.right: Between 2000 and 2020, the number of cars doubled.
examples.note: Both ends are in the past → past simple throughout.

examples.right: Since 2020, the number of cars has doubled.
The figure stood at 20% in 2010 and has remained stable since then.
examples.note: Past simple for the anchor date, present perfect for the open period.

commonMistakes.wrong: Vietnam has recorded strong growth in 2019.
commonMistakes.why: Một năm đã kết thúc thì không dùng hiện tại hoàn thành. Tiếng Việt không phân biệt thì này, nên người học hay dịch *đã* thành *have + V3*.

commonMistakes.wrong: I have seen this documentary last night.
commonMistakes.right: I saw this documentary last night.
commonMistakes.why: **last night** là thời gian đã chấm dứt. Nếu trả lời được câu hỏi *when?* bằng một mốc quá khứ thì phải dùng quá khứ đơn.

commonMistakes.wrong: The government has introduced the policy since three years.
commonMistakes.right: The government introduced the policy three years ago.
commonMistakes.why: **since** cần một điểm bắt đầu, không nhận khoảng thời gian; còn *three years ago* là mốc đã kết thúc. Chỉ dùng **for three years** khi tình huống còn tiếp diễn.

commonMistakes.wrong: Since 2015, the city invested in metro lines.
commonMistakes.right: Since 2015, the city has invested in metro lines.
commonMistakes.why: **Since + năm** mở ra một giai đoạn chưa kết thúc, nên bắt buộc dùng hiện tại hoàn thành.

commonMistakes.wrong: The rate of crime has decreased last decade.
commonMistakes.right: The rate of crime decreased last decade.
commonMistakes.why: *Last decade* là giai đoạn đã đóng. Cẩn thận với những cụm nghe như còn tiếp diễn nhưng thực ra đã kết thúc.

ieltsTips: Dùng **hiện tại hoàn thành** để mở một đoạn thân bài Task 2 về vấn đề còn tiếp diễn: *Housing affordability has deteriorated in most major cities.* Rồi chống đỡ bằng một số liệu ở **quá khứ đơn**: *In 2023, the average rent reached 45% of median income.*
Trong Task 1, chọn một thì cho cả thân bài và giữ nguyên. Giám khảo chấm cả tính nhất quán — đổi thì giữa đoạn khiến người đọc thấy bạn chưa kiểm soát được dạng thức.
Với ngôn ngữ xu hướng, `have/has + V3` đi tự nhiên với *over the past decade*, *in recent years*, *since the outbreak* — ba cụm khiến câu văn nghe thời sự và đúng chất band 8.
Đừng dùng `have been` ở mọi câu. Điểm nằm ở **độ đa dạng**: luân phiên hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn (*has been rising*) với quá khứ đơn (*rose*) khi mốc thời gian thật sự thay đổi.

exercises.question: The proportion of remote workers ___ sharply since the pandemic began.
exercises.explanation: **since the pandemic began** opens a period that continues to now → present perfect **has risen**.

exercises.question: In 2019, the government ___ a new tax on single-use plastics.
This is the highest level of air pollution the city ___ in a decade.
exercises.explanation: After **This is the highest level ...**, the experience up to now takes the present perfect.

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I have visited Da Nang last summer.
I visited Da Nang last summer.
I have been visiting Da Nang last summer.
I visit Da Nang last summer.
exercises.explanation: **last summer** is finished, so the past simple is the only correct choice.

exercises.question: Over the past twenty years, average class sizes ___ (increase) steadily.
exercises.explanation: **Over the past twenty years** reaches the present. Both the simple and continuous present perfect are natural here.

exercises.question: The council ___ (approve) the new housing plan two months ago.
exercises.explanation: **ago** always signals finished time → past simple.

exercises.question: The number of electric cars ___ (double) since 2018.
exercises.explanation: **since 2018** is an unfinished period → present perfect.

exercises.question: Between 2005 and 2015, the city ___ (build) three new metro lines.
exercises.explanation: A closed period with two past dates → past simple.

exercises.question: Researchers ___ (find) no evidence of a link so far.
exercises.explanation: **so far** means *up to now* → present perfect.

exercises.question: Choose the sentence that describes an open-ended trend.
exercises.explanation: Only **since 2020** leaves the period open, so only the present perfect is appropriate.
